title: Velocity POC — scaling & autoscale tuning sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's dedicated pool utilization, p95/p99 latency spikes during bursts, adjust autoscaling windows and burst buffer, and agree next actions: run a 2-hour synthetic surge test, share tuned autoscale policy JSON, and provide SOC2/KMS compliance notes for on-prem plan.
topics: Autoscale policy tuning (scale up/down windows, cool down)
Burst capacity planning and failover routes
KV cache and batching impact on latency
action_items: Evan: run 2-hour synthetic surge test on staging and share logs by 2026-07-02
Marco: upload recommended autoscale policy JSON to shared drive by 2026-07-01
Jamie: send pricing delta for 50% burst buffer and Dedicated reserve by 2026-07-02
Nora: add SOC2/KMS whitepaper link to the workspace and connect security contact by 2026-07-03
next_steps: Apply Marco's autoscale policy on a single worker pool in staging
If surge test passes, trial burst policy for 48 hours in lower env
Customer to confirm internal stakeholders for Dedicated commitment decision (procurement/legal)
Redwood to provide short runbook for failover to hosted model variant during saturation
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-30 11:00 PT | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Gutierrez (Redwood SE), Nora Lin (Redwood CSM), Priya Raman (Velocity Eng Manager), Evan Cho (Velocity SRE), Leah Brooks (Velocity Product)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — utilization readout, autoscale tuning, burst planning, compliance asks. priya, you good with that?
[00:20] Priya: Yep, perfect. we've got some fresh numbers from last week's load test that spiked around 2am, so eager to dig in.
[00:31] Marco: I pulled the Dedicated pool metrics, I'll share screen in a sec. note — CSVs in the shared drive, names start with vel-poc-metrics-0619.
[00:42] Evan: yeah the spike — p99 jumped to 1.2s for a short window, p95 stayed around 300-350ms. we saw KV cache cold miss rate increase.
[00:55] Marco: That aligns with the KV cache TTL expiration pattern. during the synthetic surge we didn't have the prefix cache warmed, so you lose the prefix benefits and batching falls back to smaller batch sizes.
[01:12] Leah: so are we saying it's mostly cache warming, or is it the autoscale not reacting fast enough?
[01:20] Marco: A bit of both. current autoscale policy uses a 60s evaluation window with a 120s cool-down — that is conservative and prevents flapping but makes scale-up slow during sudden bursts.
[01:34] Evan: our usual traffic model includes sharp spikes from the mobile app at top of hour, so yeah, we need faster scale-up but don't want to overprovision constantly.
[01:45] Jamie: We recommended a two-tier policy last week — a quick transient scale-up gate with a small burst buffer, plus a longer sustained scale path. do you want me to outline the numbers?
[01:57] Priya: yes please, that would help.
[02:02] Marco: proposed quick gate: if p95 CPU > 70% for two consecutive 15s samples then add one worker (warm start), with a burst buffer of 50% of baseline for 10 minutes. sustained path: if p95 > 60% for 3m then scale additional workers until p95 drops below 55%, cool-down 180s.
[02:25] Evan: hmm the 15s samples are tricky — our instrumentation aggregates at 10s but the Redwood telemetry we're seeing is 20s buckets, sometimes 30s. could cause missed triggers.
[02:38] Marco: good point. we can make the policy use service-side shorter telemetry hooks (we have a mode to evaluate lightweight probes at 10s) — that'll reduce missed triggers but slightly increase control plane churn.
[02:51] Leah: what about cost? any ballpark for enabling a 50% burst buffer for a week?
[02:58] Jamie: rough back-of-envelope — depends on baseline. for your current baseline of ~8 workers, 50% burst means +4 workers during bursts; cost delta estimate is in the pricing doc I shared, I'll send an updated line-item after the call.
[03:13] Priya: ok. Evan, do you think you can run a 2-hour surge test in staging to validate?
[03:18] Evan: yes i can schedule that. i want to run two variants: one with current autoscale policy and one with tuned policy Marco provides.
[03:27] Marco: great — i'll push a policy JSON to the shared folder. note: include a fallback rule to route to a hosted-compatible model variant when queue depth exceeds threshold to avoid tail-latency blowups.
[03:41] Priya: fallback to hosted model — is that seamless for us? any data residency concerns?
[03:47] Jamie: it depends on routing policy. we can restrict fallback to only the non-sensitive endpoints and keep PHI-bound traffic on private Dedicated nodes. also we can annotate routes with data-class to prevent cross-border issues.
[04:01] Evan: about KV cache — any quick fixes to reduce cold miss? we considered pre-warming at forecasted peak times.
[04:08] Marco: pre-warm is effective. we also recommend increasing KV cache TTL slightly for the high-frequency prefixes. tradeoff is memory usage on the worker. quantization and smaller batch sizes during surge also affect memory profile.
[04:21] Leah: Do we need to change model size or quantization to improve throughput?
[04:26] Marco: Potentially. For inference quality you wanted the bigger model, but if throughput is critical, there are compatible quantized variants we can try that reduce per-token compute by ~20-30% while keeping output quality within your eval thresholds. we should run evals against the customer prompt set.
[04:43] Priya: good. put that on the list.
[04:47] Jamie: quick security note — Nora, can you remind Velocity of the SOC2/KMS docs we promised?
[04:53] Nora: yes. i'll drop the whitepaper and a short checklist to the workspace after this call, plus contact info for the security engineer.
[04:59] Evan: thanks. also procurement asked about committed Dedicated pricing if we need a 50% burst buffer guaranteed.
[05:06] Jamie: i'll send a delta quote. we have pricing models for reserved capacity plus optional burst reserve; i'll include 3- and 12-month comparisons.
[05:18] Marco: back to autoscale specifics — one more operational suggestion: enable rate-limiter fallback across routes so that if one pool is saturated we can degrade non-critical routes gracefully instead of causing global p99 spikes.
[05:33] Priya: makes sense. Leah, from product perspective, which routes are non-critical?
[05:38] Leah: analytics and low-priority background summary jobs. core user-facing completion must be highest.
[05:45] Marco: we'll add those labels to the sample rollout config.
[05:48] Evan: about the surge test — i propose we run it Wednesday night at 02:00 for 2 hours. that mirrors production pattern.
[05:55] Priya: works for me.
[05:58] Marco: i'll be available to watch logs and adjust policy live if needed.
[06:02] Jamie: perfect. next, any questions on networking — VPC peering, routes?
[06:08] Evan: we're seeing occasional 5XXs during cold starts that look like TLS handshake timeouts on the peered connection during scale events. maybe connection churn.
[06:18] Marco: that can happen when workers are added and the connection pool is rebuilt. we recommend connection warmers and increasing connection pool size in the proxy to reduce transient TLS handshake errors.
[06:30] Priya: is there tooling to observe those handshake failures in Redwood Console?
[06:34] Marco: yes, per-route TCP error metrics are available; i'll point to the dashboard. also there's a trace hook you can enable for 5 minutes during the surge to capture handshake latencies.
[06:46] Leah: would enabling that trace hook impact latency?
[06:49] Marco: negligible for short runs, it's sampling-based.
[06:52] Evan: anything else we should validate in the surge test? I'd like to capture CPU, GPU util, batch sizes, queue depth and KV hit ratio.
[07:01] Marco: perfect list. also capture token-per-second and per-model variant latency.
[07:06] Priya: okay. can we have a quick recap of responsibilities?
[07:09] Jamie: sure — Evan runs surge test and shares logs by Friday; Marco uploads autoscale JSON and the fallback config by Thursday; Jamie sends burst pricing and runbook for hosted fallback by Friday; Nora posts SOC2/KMS docs by Saturday.
[07:25] Priya: good. any blockers to running the tests?
[07:28] Evan: none on our side. just need the policy JSON and a short runbook for how to flip policies in staging.
[07:35] Marco: will include the exact commands and an example curl to flip the policy, plus rollback steps.
[07:42] Leah: wondering about alerting thresholds — what should our SRE alerts look like for early warning?
[07:47] Marco: recommend two tiers: early-warning when p95 CPU > 60% for 3m or queue depth > 100, critical when p99 latency > 1s or queue depth > 500. hook those to PagerDuty.
[07:59] Evan: agreed. we'll draft the alert runbook and share.
[08:03] Jamie: quick note for procurement: if you need an enterprise SLA and on-prem Private offering, that shifts lead time a bit — we'll connect Legal if you go down that path.
[08:12] Priya: we're evaluating both Dedicated with burst reserve and a Private on-prem option. procurement will decide after the surge validation.
[08:21] Nora: i'll coordinate a security review call if you want to fast-track SOC2 evidence.
[08:25] Leah: yes let's do that, probably next week.
[08:29] Jamie: ok final recap in chat — action items and next steps, and i'll send meeting notes. thanks all.
[08:36] Priya: thanks.
[48:00] [call end]

Notes: transcript includes stutters, overlapping speech at times, and a few mis-heard tokens in the raw export (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" in earlier auto transcript).
